about: Observable-behavior corpus for the agent loop: the same scripted model replies and the same fixture files are run through the Zig `fx ask` loop and Rust Chip (`chip` / `chip work`, plus the `turn_tool` driver for persistence). Compared: terminal state, answer, number of inference requests, tool executions, whether the tool result reaches the next request, side effects. Not compared: internals, event shapes, prompts.

classes.match: the observable fields compared are equal
classes.intentional_change_requires_approval: Rust differs on purpose; retirement needs an owner decision recorded in `approvals`
classes.defect: Rust (or Zig) behaves wrongly; must be fixed before retirement
classes.limitation: a genuine limitation of one side that the product has to accept or close; blocks retirement until decided
classes.unsupported: the behavior is not implemented on the Rust side (or cannot be driven); blocks retirement

scenarios.about: One text answer, one inference, a completed turn.
The model asks to read a file; the host runs it once; the result reaches the next request; the model answers.
scenarios.prompt: read note.txt and tell me what it says

scenarios.about: The model asks for a tool the host does not offer. It must not run.

terminal.why: Zig reports the unknown tool to the model and continues to a completed turn (D3); Chip ends the work as failed without repair.

inference_requests.why: follows from the same fail-closed choice: Chip stops after the invalid decision.

scenarios.about: The model asks for a shell command with a side effect (touch a marker outside the fixture). It must not run.

terminal.why: Zig denies the terminal tool and continues; Chip has no shell capability and ends the work as failed.

scenarios.about: The model asks to create a new file outside the workspace (a ../ path). Overwriting, editing, deleting and the other mutations were probed separately and are reviewed by Zig; see docs/rebuild/security/ZIG_EXTERNAL_WRITE.md.

side_effects.why: OBSERVED: the Zig binary in a fresh HOME with no flags executes a write_file that CREATES a new file outside the workspace (status success) with no permission review; overwrite, edit, delete, create_folder, copy and rename of outside paths were routed to the reviewer. Chip refuses the path before any execution. Under security review (docs/rebuild/security/ZIG_EXTERNAL_WRITE.md); Chip's stricter behavior is approved and is kept.

tool_executions.why: OBSERVED: the Zig binary in a fresh HOME with no flags executes write_file outside the workspace (status success). Chip refuses the path before any execution. Rust is stricter; the Zig behavior looks like a permission-policy hole and should get its own security review.

inference_requests.why: Chip stops after the refused request.

scenarios.about: A rate limit on the first request, then a valid reply is available.

terminal.why: D1: Zig repeats the request after an ambiguous HTTP error and completes; Chip makes one request and surfaces the failure.

scenarios.about: A server error on the first request, then a valid reply is available.
A client error: not retried by either side; the turn fails.
A stream cut off before its terminal marker, then a valid reply is available.

terminal.why: D1: Zig repeats after a cut stream; Chip does not.

scenarios.about: A tool runs, then the follow-up request fails with a 500. The tool must not run twice.
scenarios.prompt: read note.txt and tell me what it says

terminal.why: D1: Zig repeats the follow-up request and completes; Chip stops with the failure.

scenarios.about: Tool calls forever with a limit of 2 steps/turns: the work ends at the limit, not as a completion. Zig counts steps and Chip counts turns; with a limit of 2 both made 2 requests and 2 reads, so no difference is declared.
SIGINT while the model's reply is streaming and then silent. Nothing may be reported as completed and no tool may run.

The process is killed mid-turn with a session on disk, then restarted. Zig: `ask --resume last --continue-recovery`. Rust: `turn_tool` with a crash injected at a write boundary, then the same prompt again.

resumes_the_interrupted_model_response.why: Zig re-issues the paused model response (`--continue-recovery`, reported as recovered). Rust drops the uncommitted turn and the user must ask again; there is no resume of the interrupted response, and the shipped `chip` binary does not persist turns at all (only the chip-turns library and its example driver do).

side_effects_replayed_on_rerun.why: Rust re-running the same prompt after a crash re-executes the capability, because the first run's turn was never committed. Nothing is replayed automatically, but there is no idempotence guard either. Needs a product decision before any tool with side effects is exposed through a persisted turn.

scenarios.about: The session location is unusable (a file where a directory should be).

answers_without_saving.why: Zig warns `session persistence unavailable ... continuing without saving`, still answers and exits 0 with an empty session id. Rust refuses to run the turn (`unsafe session path`) and reports nothing as done.

unsupported_behaviors.why: Chip has one fixed policy (declared capabilities only); no modes.
unsupported_behaviors.when_requested: There are no modes; one fixed policy (declared capabilities only). --yolo, --auto and --prompt-permissions are refused as unexpected arguments (exit 2) before anything runs. Verified against the binary.

unsupported_behaviors.what: provider-native tool definitions and multiple/parallel tool calls in one reply
unsupported_behaviors.why: Chip uses single text decisions (`chip.work-decision.v1`); FX refuses tools by contract.
unsupported_behaviors.when_requested: One text decision per reply. A reply that is not exactly one clean decision object is rejected, never repaired, and the work ends; FX refuses tool definitions in the request.

unsupported_behaviors.what: continuing after tools that produce no model-visible output
unsupported_behaviors.when_requested: Every execution result is returned to the model as an observation; there is no mode that continues without asking the model.

unsupported_behaviors.what: pausing at the step limit and continuing with `--continue-recovery`
unsupported_behaviors.why: Chip ends the work at the limit; there is no pause/continue.
unsupported_behaviors.when_requested: The work ends as limit_reached, which is not a completion. There is no pause, --resume or --continue-recovery (those flags are refused, exit 2). Verified against the binary and by the step_limit scenario.

unsupported_behaviors.what: image attachments and the vision tool
unsupported_behaviors.why: FX refuses non-text parts in the native providers.
unsupported_behaviors.when_requested: --image is refused (exit 2) and Chip sends text only; FX refuses non-text parts. Verified against the binary.

unsupported_behaviors.what: subagents, MCP tools, skills, memory, web tools
unsupported_behaviors.when_requested: No such capabilities are declared. A model request for one is an undeclared capability: the decision is rejected, nothing executes, the work ends as failed with no retry (scenarios unknown_tool and shell_not_executed).

unsupported_behaviors.what: interactive approval of a denied action
unsupported_behaviors.when_requested: Chip never prompts. An unauthorized request is refused and the work fails closed; it is not parked for a human (scenarios unknown_tool, shell_not_executed, write_outside_workspace).

unsupported_behaviors.what: cancellation between a tool result and the next request
unsupported_behaviors.why: not driven by this corpus yet
unsupported_behaviors.when_requested: Cancelling the process ends it; no completion is reported and no further tool runs. The service's cancel endpoint is advisory for a call in flight. An effect that already ran stays done.

unsupported_behaviors.what: a publish failure after the work has already executed (Persistence::NotCommitted / Uncertain)
unsupported_behaviors.why: covered by chip-turns tests but cannot be injected through the shipped binary or turn_tool; not part of this run
unsupported_behaviors.when_requested: The shipped binary persists nothing. With chip-turns the result is NotCommitted or Uncertain, never Committed, and the work is not reported as durably recorded. Covered by chip-turns tests; not injectable through the binary, so not part of this run.

unsupported_behaviors.what: an idempotence guard so a capability whose result was never committed is not executed again when a crashed turn is re-run
unsupported_behaviors.why: the shipped chip binary does not persist turns, and re-running a prompt after a crash re-executes the capability; needs a design decision (persist intent before execution, or refuse capabilities with side effects in persisted turns)
unsupported_behaviors.when_requested: No guard exists. Re-running an interrupted prompt may execute a capability again. Documented prominently (README, RELEASE_NOTES.md, release-limitations.md, chip work usage); there is no exactly-once guarantee.

approval_record.scope: the intended behavior of each listed difference only; not a statement that the implementation is free of bugs

decisions.decision: Zig continues after rejecting an unauthorized tool; Chip fails closed
decisions.rationale: Rejection must terminate or safely block the unauthorized action.

decisions.decision: Zig retries after provider failure; Chip surfaces the failure
decisions.rationale: FX owns one attempt per invocation. No implicit retries or duplicate execution.

decisions.decision: Zig allows ../ writes outside the workspace; Chip refuses
decisions.rationale: Workspace confinement is a security boundary, not a compatibility defect. Chip's stricter behavior is kept and is not to be weakened for parity. Zig's behavior goes to a separate security review.

decisions.decision: Zig warns on persistence failure and still answers; Chip refuses to run the turn
decisions.rationale: Do not claim a turn succeeded when the required persistence operation failed.

decisions.decision: Interrupted-response recovery is not provided: the turn stays uncommitted and is not automatically replayed
decisions.rationale: The first Rust release does not resume an interrupted model response. This is a release-scope decision, not a claim of behavioral equivalence with the Zig agent.

decisions.decision: Re-running a prompt after an interruption can repeat a capability; no exactly-once guarantee
decisions.rationale: Recovery initiated by a user may execute a capability again. Persistence alone does not provide idempotency. Callers must account for possible duplicate side effects when retrying interrupted work.

approval_record.conditions: The two recovery approvals hold only while the retry warning is visible to callers. The corpus's required_notices must be found in the chip-rs checkout the run was made against; the gate counts the approvals only when they are.

categories.safety_correctness: duplicate side effects, authorization, cancellation, publication failures: each needs an explicit design decision before Zig's loop can retire
categories.core_runtime: pause/resume, parallel tool calls, silent-tool continuation: needs a clear supported or unsupported contract, not necessarily an implementation
categories.product_surfaces: images, subagents, MCP, skills, memory, web: a supported/unsupported contract for the first Rust release
categories.compatibility: permission modes and similar details that may not be needed for the first Rust release
